judgements.reason: Multiquadratic has essentially nothing left: the baseline already has the narrow 2-rank formula for both signatures, the ambiguous class number formula and Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl/Cl^2. ConformalMapping still has to prove the global Schwarz–Christoffel theorem (injectivity and image equal to the polygon) and the parameter problem, although it can build on the existing Riemann-mapping, Carathéodory and reflection results.

Beyond generator and check matrices, Coding Theory must build all of duality (Euclidean and Hermitian), weight enumerators and MacWilliams, Type II codes, the explicit tetracode/hexacode/Golay computations, Construction A and the discriminant-module bridge: six largely unbuilt layers. ConformalMapping lacks only the final Schwarz–Christoffel layer.

Chebotarev needs a deeper stack. It imports GlobalNumberFields' power-saving ray-class lattice-point counts, then must build continuation and nonvanishing of cyclotomic character series near Re s = 1, the abelian and general density theorems, a Wiener–Ikehara weighted crossing and the prime ideal theorem for K. Coding Theory's missing layers (duality, MacWilliams, Golay codes, Construction A) are broad but elementary finite algebra on an already complete lattice library.

Chebotarev's gap is the imported ray-class ideal counting plus about ten layers of analytic assembly, and the baseline already has Artin symbols, Frobenius prime sets, Wiener–Ikehara, prime-count transfers and Dirichlet density. PadicMeasures has less underneath (abstract measures, the Z_p-only Amice transform, Weierstrass preparation). It must build completed group rings and convolution, general Amice theory with φ/ψ, the Λ-module structure theorem with characteristic and Fitting ideals, determinant functors on perfect complexes and Gorenstein duality, plus rigid weight spaces that need missing rigid-analytic foundations.

GlobalNumberFields still lacks many layers: power-saving ray-class counting, adelic compactness and strong approximation, the idele class group dictionary, adele base change, Hecke characters and infinity types, and orders with Picard groups. But these are textbook foundations on Mathlib's adele and fundamental-cone API and its finished ray-class layer. PadicMeasures stacks more advanced new theory with less support: completed group rings, the Iwasawa structure theorem and characteristic ideals, Knudsen–Mumford determinants of perfect complexes, Gorenstein-order duality and rigid weight spaces requiring rigid geometry that does not yet exist.

GlobalNumberFields' remaining layers (ray-class lattice counting, adeles and ideles, Hecke characters, orders and Picard groups) are foundational and build on Mathlib's adele and fundamental-cone API. GeometryOfNumbers must build much deeper theory: Minkowski's second theorem, Hasse–Minkowski over number fields (which needs class-field-theoretic reciprocity), genera and spinor genera, the Siegel mass formula and theta series, unipotent-flow and nondivergence dynamics for Oppenheim/Duke-type results, LLL, and higher hermitian K-theory on imported algebraic K-theory.

ShimuraData's gap is a single coherent stack: Weil restriction and adelic points, Cartan involutions and Hermitian symmetric domains, variations of Hodge structure with compact duals and reflex fields, then the datum category and examples. GeometryOfNumbers needs several independent deep theories: local–global quadratic forms through Hasse–Minkowski and spinor genera, mass formulas and theta series, homogeneous dynamics (Ratner-type unipotent flows, Dani–Margulis), and Grothendieck–Witt theory on imported algebraic K-theory and spectra.

Logic must build valued-field model theory (AKE, Denef–Pas elimination), p-adic cell decomposition and Igusa rationality, and Cluckers–Loeser motivic integration, which imports geometric mixed motives and, through them, K-theory, stacks and intersection theory. It also needs MRDP and o-minimality with Pila–Wilkie and André–Oort cases. ShimuraData's missing Lie-group, Hermitian-domain, Hodge-variation and flag-variety layers are a smaller and shallower stack.

BelyiMaps' gap is long but classical: triangle groups, van Kampen and π1 ≅ F2, analytic Riemann existence resting on imported compact-Riemann-surface cohomology, algebraization, Belyi's theorem, fields of moduli and the branch-cycle and pro-ℓ arguments. Logic requires research-level theories that are absent together with their foundations: Denef–Pas quantifier elimination and p-adic integration, motivic integration importing mixed motives, and o-minimal geometry with Pila–Wilkie counting and André–Oort cases.

BelyiMaps needs classical covering-space, Riemann-surface and profinite-group theory. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs overconvergent cohomology of arithmetic groups over number fields (BSW), Hilbert modular q-expansion theory (Deligne–Ribet), CM abelian varieties with Igusa towers and p-adic differential operators (Katz, Hsieh), and unitary Shimura varieties with toroidal compactifications and doubling integrals (EHLS). On top of that it imports Iwasawa algebras, eigenvarieties and Euler-system roadmaps: about 559 stages across 83 roadmaps.

PadicDifferentialEquations needs Robba rings, Kedlaya's local monodromy theorem, rigid cohomology with finiteness and p-adic Weil II, on top of imported Weil I and crystalline cohomology. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs four monograph-scale constructions (BSW overconvergent cohomology over number fields, Deligne–Ribet/Katz with Igusa towers and p-adic differential operators, Hsieh, and EHLS on compactified unitary Shimura varieties). Its import graph (559 stages, 83 roadmaps, depth 23) even contains part of the p-adic-cohomology stack itself.

Both sit on vast absent stacks: CohomologyComparisons imports A_inf and prismatic cohomology, de Rham–Witt/log-crystalline/Hyodo–Kato theory and perfectoid geometry, while PadicDifferentialEquations imports all of ℓ-adic étale cohomology through Weil I plus crystalline basics and dagger geometry. The difference is in the roadmaps' own layers. CohomologyComparisons mostly assembles comparisons from maps its suppliers construct. PadicDifferentialEquations must itself build Robba-ring theory and Kedlaya's local monodromy theorem, rigid cohomology from frames up, finiteness with alterations and duality, and p-adic Weil II.

CohomologyComparisons needs the integral p-adic Hodge stack (A_inf, prismatic, crystalline, perfectoid) plus its comparison layers. Excursion operators need the whole Fargues–Scholze geometrization on the same perfectoid/diamond base: local shtukas, Bun_G strata, geometric Satake, lisse v-stack sheaves and Langlands parameter stacks. They also need Weil II with hard Lefschetz, the classical GL_n correspondence and function-field automorphic theory, and then the spectral action itself (324 imported stages across 52 roadmaps).

Both are at the far end. Excursion operators need the full Fargues–Scholze machinery (local shtukas, Bun_G, geometric Satake, parameter stacks, Weil II) plus the categorical action and GL_n/LRS comparisons. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs four separate monograph-scale constructions (BSW, Deligne–Ribet/Katz/Hsieh, EHLS, Eischen–Wan) and imports Shimura compactifications, Igusa towers, eigenvarieties, Iwasawa theory and much of the same étale and p-adic geometry (559 stages over 83 roadmaps against 324 over 52).

Multiquadratic's genus theory is essentially complete in the baseline, including the 2-rank formulas and Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl/Cl^2. Chebotarev still needs the imported power-saving ray-class ideal counts, continuation and nonvanishing of character series, the abelian and general density theorems, the Wiener–Ikehara weighted transfer and the prime ideal theorem for K.

ConformalMapping lacks only the global Schwarz–Christoffel theorem and its parameter problem, on top of an existing Riemann-mapping/Carathéodory/reflection library. GlobalNumberFields still has about nine unbuilt layers: power-saving ray-class lattice counting, finite and full adeles with compactness and strong approximation, the idele class group and ray-class dictionary, adele base change, Hecke characters and infinity types, cyclotomic arithmetic, and orders with Pic/NarrowPic.

PadicDifferentialEquations builds rigid cohomology, Kedlaya's local monodromy and p-adic Weil II on imported Weil I and crystalline cohomology. Excursion operators import a larger étale stack (Weil II with hard Lefschetz, perverse sheaves, vanishing cycles) together with the entire Fargues–Scholze geometrization: perfectoid spaces and diamonds, local shtukas, Bun_G, geometric Satake, parameter stacks. They also need the classical GL_n correspondence and function-field automorphic theory, and only then construct the spectral action.

Both carry several research-scale theories: GeometryOfNumbers has Hasse–Minkowski with its reciprocity input, mass formulas and theta series, Ratner-type dynamics for Oppenheim/Duke, and hermitian K-theory. Logic has AKE/Denef–Pas elimination, p-adic and motivic integration, MRDP, and o-minimality with Pila–Wilkie and André–Oort cases. Logic's import graph (42 stages, depth 11) contains GeometryOfNumbers' K-theory imports (19 stages) and adds geometric mixed motives, motivic cohomology, algebraic stacks and intersection theory, which tips the balance.

PadicMeasures has one geometric layer (rigid weight spaces) among mostly algebraic ones: completed group rings, the Iwasawa structure theorem and characteristic ideals, determinant functors and Gorenstein duality. ShimuraData stacks more geometry: imported Weil restriction, adelic group points and flag schemes, then real Lie structure theory (Cartan involutions, compact real forms) for Hermitian symmetric domains, variations of Hodge structure, compact duals with reflex-field descent, and the datum category with Siegel/Hilbert examples. That is a somewhat larger and deeper gap.

Coding Theory's missing layers (duality, MacWilliams, Type II and Golay codes, Construction A, discriminant bridge) are elementary finite algebra on a complete lattice library. BelyiMaps must stack triangle groups, van Kampen and cover classification, branched-cover compactification, and Riemann existence resting on imported compact-Riemann-surface cohomology and function-field Riemann–Roch. It then needs algebraization, Belyi's theorem with descent, fields of moduli, the profinite π1 comparison, the branch-cycle theorem and pro-ℓ faithfulness.

CohomologyComparisons needs the A_inf/prismatic/crystalline/perfectoid stack plus its comparison layers. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions' import graph already contains CohomologyComparisons stages and most of that p-adic geometry, and it adds Shimura varieties with toroidal compactifications and Igusa towers, eigenvarieties, Iwasawa algebras and Euler systems. It also has four monograph-scale p-adic L-function constructions of its own (BSW, Deligne–Ribet/Katz/Hsieh, EHLS, Eischen–Wan).

ConformalMapping lacks only the global Schwarz–Christoffel theorem and the parameter problem, on an existing Riemann-mapping and boundary-correspondence library. PadicMeasures has almost everything still to build: completed group rings and convolution, general Amice theory with φ/ψ, pseudo-measures, the Iwasawa structure theorem with characteristic and Fitting ideals, determinant functors, Gorenstein duality and rigid weight spaces.

Coding Theory needs elementary finite algebra (duality, MacWilliams, explicit Golay codes, Construction A) on a complete lattice library. Logic needs valued-field quantifier elimination, p-adic and motivic integration with imported motives and stacks, the full MRDP theorem, and o-minimal geometry with Pila–Wilkie counting and André–Oort cases.

GlobalNumberFields' gap is broad but foundational: ray-class lattice counting, adeles and ideles, Hecke characters and infinity types, and orders with Picard groups, on Mathlib's adele API and a finished ray-class layer. BelyiMaps stacks many more layers: triangle groups, van Kampen and cover classification, compactification, analytic Riemann existence on imported compact-Riemann-surface cohomology, algebraization with function-field Riemann–Roch, and Belyi's theorem with descent. It then needs fields of moduli, the profinite π1 comparison with ẑ-powers, the branch-cycle theorem and pro-ℓ faithfulness.
